subject: Archaeology
title: The Palace of Knossos
description: Learn The Palace of Knossos in one minute.

hook.text: On Crete, Arthur Evans uncovered a palace so complex that it may have inspired the myth of the Labyrinth.

buildup.text: The Minoan palace at Knossos had 1,300 rooms, running water, and vivid frescoes of bull-leaping.

discovery.text: Evans revealed a civilization older than Classical Greece — the Minoans, Europe's first great culture.

twist.text: Evans rebuilt much of the palace in concrete, adding his own guesses. Scholars still debate the accuracy.

climax.text: His reconstruction created the Knossos tourists see today — part ancient ruin, part modern invention.

punchline.text: The palace that inspired the Labyrinth myth is itself a maze of fact and.

quiz.question: What controversy surrounds Evans's work at Knossos?
options: He secretly sold artifacts to private collectors
He rebuilt much of the palace in concrete based on guesses
He claimed the Minoans were Greek, which was proven false
